How rcs is tested

Source: vignettes/articles/testing.Rmd
testing.Rmd

A storage package must not lose or mix up data, also when a network fails halfway through a write. This article describes how the tests of rcs check that, and how to run them. The code below is not run here: it starts the test suite, which takes from seconds to many minutes depending on the level.

Two rules hold throughout the suite:

  • every algorithm is compared with a slow, independent reference;
  • every operation on a store is followed by a check of the store’s invariants.

All tests use simulated data from the rcs_sim_*() generators, and every store is built in temporary folders that are removed afterwards. The tests use testthat (third edition).

Test levels

The suite has three levels, chosen by the environment variable RCS_TEST_LEVEL. Each level adds tests to the one before.

Level What it runs Default when
cran Unit tests and small property tests (4 to 30 random cases each): no network, small data, a few seconds per file. RCS_TEST_LEVEL is unset and the tests run on CRAN or under R CMD check.
default Adds the integration suite on local folders and property tests of about 200 random cases each. RCS_TEST_LEVEL is unset otherwise, e.g. under devtools::test().
full Adds property tests of up to 2,000 cases, every point of every crash-point matrix, the long random-operation sequences, and the tests against a Google Cloud Storage bucket. Never; set it.

Run each level from the package folder:

# default: the local integration suite and property tests
devtools::test()

# cran: unit tests and small property tests
withr::with_envvar(c(RCS_TEST_LEVEL = "cran"), devtools::test())

# full: everything, including the random-operation test
withr::with_envvar(c(RCS_TEST_LEVEL = "full"), devtools::test())

# one file
devtools::test(filter = "intersects")

Inside the tests, skip_below_level("default") or skip_below_level("full") at the top of a test skips it below that level, and property_cases() gives the number of random cases of a property test at the current level. Both live in tests/testthat/helper-levels.R.

Store invariants

After every step of every integration test, expect_store_valid(st) (tests/testthat/helper-invariants.R) reads the catalogs of every available location again and checks, for each:

  1. every file the catalog names (current and history) exists, with the recorded size and MD5 checksum, and its Parquet footer holds the recorded number of rows;
  2. every dataset’s version equals the hash of its file rows, and its totals (files, rows, bytes) equal the sums of those rows;
  3. a manifest exists for every version in the catalog and agrees with it, and no file is named by two datasets;
  4. with history off, no file exists that the catalog does not name, apart from files left by an injected failure, which store_prune() must then remove;
  5. every index table agrees with its dataset: every row identifier exists and every recorded main cell equals the row’s h3;
  6. every secondary copy of a dataset either equals the primary’s or is reported as missing, primary only or differs by store_status().

It also checks that the connection object holds the catalogs that are stored, so that a function that changed a location updated the object in place. All problems are collected and reported in one failure.

Failures and crash points

A backend stub (tests/testthat/helper-backend-stub.R) wraps the local backend, counts the calls made through it and, on chosen calls, fails or silently alters a written file. With it the tests check, among others:

  • a failure of the primary during upload, or between two catalog files: no catalog changes, and repeating the call succeeds and copies only what is missing;
  • a failure of a secondary during a write: a warning, the secondary is reported as behind, and store_sync() with the dataset named in datasets, or with all = TRUE, repairs it (a plain store_sync() would not copy a dataset that the secondary never received);
  • a transient error on the first two attempts of one file: the write succeeds;
  • an upload that silently alters a file: the MD5 check stops the write;
  • a catalog changed by another writer between the start of a write and its catalog switch: the write stops and changes nothing;
  • a stale lock on a local location is taken over, a fresh one blocks;
  • a lock that cannot be released after a catalog switch only warns: the operation completes, secondaries included, and the lock stays until its timeout;
  • a reader connected before a write reads the old version when history is kept, and without history gets an error (class rcs_error_version_not_found) telling it to run store_refresh().

The crash-point matrix goes through the backend calls of an operation. Each of store_write() (every mode, and a geospatial write with its index table), store_sync(), store_delete() and store_prune() is first run with a counting stub to learn its number of backend calls, N. It is then run again with the stub failing at one call, on the primary and on a secondary: at level full at every call 1, 2, …, N; at level default at one call of some of the matrices, plus every be_unlock() call. After each failure the invariants hold, every location holds the old or the new version of each dataset and never a mixture, and repeating the call (or store_sync(all = TRUE) for a secondary left behind by a write) succeeds, sends only the files that are missing, and ends in the state of a run without failure. Orphans left by the failure are then removed by store_prune().

The matrix is the helper crash_matrix() in tests/testthat/helper-model.R; a test file calls it like this:

crash_matrix("store_sync()",
  setup = function(paths) { ... },   # builds the start state in three folders
  op = function(st) store_sync(st, all = TRUE),  # the operation on a connection
  stub_at = 1L,                      # 1: fail in the primary, 2: in a secondary
  points = NULL,                     # NULL: every call; a number: that many
  repair = "repeat",                 # what follows a failure
  unlock = TRUE                      # also fail every be_unlock() call
)

The random-operation test

Seeded sequences of operations run against three local locations and, in parallel, against a plain model in memory: a named list of data frames per location. Level default runs two short sequences of 6 operations; level full runs four sequences of 50 (tests/testthat/test-random-operations.R, with the helper random_sequence() in helper-model.R). The operations are create, replace, update, delete, sync, copy, prune, rebuild, an injected failure, and switching history on or off for the store, the connection or one dataset. After every step the invariants hold, and store_read() of every dataset from every location equals the model. A failing run prints its seed and its list of operations, so it can be replayed.

Reference oracles

The algorithms of the package are checked against slow references that share no code with it (tests/testthat/helper-geo-reference.R and the tests themselves):

  • the h3 cell of every simulated row equals the cell of largest overlap found by brute force, by intersecting the geometry with every nearby cell on the sphere;
  • the index table’s rows equal the cells a brute-force intersection with the cell grid finds, for every row that crosses a cell edge;
  • the cells computed for a query contain every cell that intersects the query shape, on the sphere and in the plane, among the cells of a dense grid of points around it, for random shapes including thin strips, large rectangles with four vertices, shapes with holes and single points;
  • a spatial read returns exactly the rows of sf::st_filter() on the whole dataset, for random query shapes and H3 cells of resolutions 2 to 9, and a superset with exact = FALSE; repeated for a projected CRS, for partitioned and unpartitioned datasets, for geocode = FALSE, for points and lines, and with sf::sf_use_s2() on and off;
  • the polygons across the antimeridian and around the pole get the brute-force cells, are found from either side of ±180° and at the pole, and are not returned by a query elsewhere;
  • a round trip of every column type (logical, integer, double, text with non-ASCII characters, factors with unused levels, ordered factors, dates, times with time zones, time differences, 64-bit integers, list columns, missing values, zero rows, every geometry type) is identical() after normalisation, for one file and for partitioned datasets;
  • the geocoding engines (tests/testthat/test-geo-engine.R) are compared with brute force on the sphere and in the plane, for two polygons that are valid in the plane but invalid on the sphere (a duplicated vertex and a spike) and for a polygon with long edges, whose cells on the sphere and in the plane differ. These geometries are given as WKT in tests/testthat/helper-geo-invalid.R, with the brute-force references for both readings. The tests also check the planar fallback of "auto" (with the rebuild mocked to return an empty or a wrong geometry), that an invalid row leaves the other rows of its chunk unchanged, that inside rows and rows across the antimeridian or around a pole get the same cells from every engine, and determinism. The read side (test-intersects.R) checks that the exact test follows the engine recorded with each dataset, and the explicit overrides.

Other checks

  • Detection: an altered data file, a missing data file, a truncated catalog, a wrong MD5 in the catalog and a manifest that disagrees with the catalog are each caught by store_check(), with a message naming the file.
  • Determinism: the same data written twice, with the same name and metadata, give the same version; changing one value changes it. The files embed the dataset’s metadata (name, title, key, partition and more), so the same rows under another name or title give another version.
  • Work counters: with options(rcs.trace = TRUE) the package counts backend calls, files opened, row groups and rows (see rcs_trace()). Because the counts are exact, tests assert them: listing and describing a store open no data file, a filter on partition columns opens only the matching files, a repeated identical write uploads no data file.
  • Messages: print methods, write summaries and error messages are covered by snapshot tests (expect_snapshot()).
  • Interoperability (tests/testthat/test-interop.R, level default): DuckDB with its spatial extension reads a written geospatial file as a geometry column with its CRS, and a filter on the bbox struct returns the rows of the same filter in R; GDAL (sf::st_read()) reads the file when its Parquet driver is present. Each test skips when its tool is missing; common Windows builds of GDAL lack the Parquet driver.

Credentials, cells, types and verbs

  • Credentials (tests/testthat/test-auth.R) run offline: the network calls, the clock and GDAL’s configuration go through small internal functions that the tests mock. They cover the default lookup order of rcs_auth_gcs(), both key types, renewal five minutes before expiry, a token that is never renewed, the GDAL options set for each credential type and the warning on a switch, the temporary DuckDB secret, and store_auth_check() with each client failing in turn. Most tests (those of the lookup, the key types, renewal, print(), str(), GDAL’s options, the DuckDB secret and store_auth_check() with failing clients) assert that no environment variable changed. The tests of the default lookup, of key types, of the same source and of print() fail on any network call; the print() and str() tests assert that no token, refresh token or client secret is shown.
  • H3 cells (test-h3-type.R): the class rcs_h3 prints hex in vectors, tibbles and sf; never fails on any 64-bit value; keeps its class through subsetting, c(), unique(), sort() and the dplyr and vctrs verbs, with NA filled as NA; and rcs_h3_hex() accepts every input form, warns for doubles and gives the same strings as the DuckDB macro.
  • Types (test-types.R): store_restore_types() on data read by arrow::read_parquet() from a dataset’s files restores factors, ordered factors, time differences, 64-bit integers, lists and cells, and leaves incompatible columns alone.
  • Geospatial verbs (test-geo-verbs.R): rcs_geo_add() and rcs_geo_index() equal what a write computes, rcs_geo_strip() undoes rcs_geo_add() exactly, and the round trip raw, prepared, written, collected and stripped gives the raw data back (attributes, identical WKB, CRS) for points, lines and polygons. Prepared writes, accepted when equal and refused when changed, are tested in test-write.R.
  • Sync (test-sync.R): syncs from the primary and from a secondary, the default scope (a secondary gets only the datasets it holds, and the call says what it left out) against all = TRUE and datasets =, deletions with and without force, a conflict (target newer) and an overwrite (source newer), dry runs, and one injected failure per phase, after which the invariants hold and a repeat sends only what is missing.
  • Copy on read (test-copy-on-read.R): with a simulated cloud primary, store_read() copies a dataset to an empty or outdated local secondary and then reads from it, sending only the changed files after an update; the size limit, copy = TRUE and copy = FALSE, and store_connect(copy_on_read = FALSE); old versions, copied only with copy = TRUE and then into the history; no copy without an eligible secondary, to a secondary holding a newer version, or by store_sample(), store_glimpse(), store_open(), store_duckdb() and reads of an index table; two secondaries served by one download; a dataset’s index table and a raster copied whole; a failing copy that warns while the read goes on; a windowed read of a class map; and one test against a bucket primary at level full.
  • Primary-only datasets (test-primary-only.R): a write with locations = "primary" lands in the primary only, contacts no secondary and records the setting (for a geospatial dataset on its index table too), which later writes keep until locations = "all"; the status primary only in store_status(), store_datasets(), the print and store_describe(); a secondary that already holds the dataset left as it was, with one message; store_sync(), with and without all = TRUE, leaving the dataset out, and datasets = copying it; reads of a raster and of a class map window that never copy it unless copy = TRUE, and one test against a bucket at level full; no notice of an empty secondary when the primary holds only such datasets.

DuckDB

The DuckDB tests skip when duckdb or DBI is missing. They make every connection through the helper local_duckdb() (tests/testthat/helper-duckdb.R), with bigint = "integer64" and closed when the test ends; local_duckdb_spatial() loads DuckDB’s spatial extension and skips when it cannot be installed (it needs a download on first use).

  • test-duckdb.R: one view per dataset in both modes, their names, the tables rcs.views and rcs.store, column types and rows equal to the Arrow reads, the guards on view names and connections, and store_tables().
  • test-duckdb-file.R: a database file whose views and user tables survive closing and reopening, refreshing after writes and deletions in the store, reconnecting from the file alone, the local-first workflow with the credential functions mocked to fail (they are never called), and a file that stays small because views hold query text only.
  • test-duckdb-tbl.R: store_open(engine = "duckdb"), whose collect() restores the R types and returns the rows of the Arrow engine.
  • test-duckdb-intersects.R: store_intersects() on DuckDB tables returns exactly the rows of the Arrow path, for cells, thin strips, polygons with holes, boxes and the antimeridian, in both modes.
  • test-write-duckdb.R: store_write() of a DuckDB table gives the same files, catalog rows, manifest and version as a write of the same data collected into R (byte for byte), checks keys and partitions inside DuckDB, and drops its temporary table also after an error.

The cloud tests

At level full, the Google Cloud Storage backend is tested against a real bucket when the environment variable RCS_TEST_GCS names one (tests/testthat/test-backend-gcs.R): uploads, downloads, MD5 checksums read without a download, listing and deletion, a Parquet file streamed through Arrow, a file read through GDAL’s /vsigs/ path, and a store on the bucket that renews an expired token; a raster is opened through /vsigs/ (test-raster.R); a store on the bucket passes store_auth_check() for every client and reads a raster through GDAL (test-auth.R); DuckDB views read the bucket’s files with a secret (test-duckdb.R); and syncs run with the bucket as a secondary (test-sync.R). All of them use the credentials of the default lookup of rcs_auth_gcs(), GDAL included, with one exception: the GDAL test of test-backend-gcs.R sets GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS to gcloud’s application-default login for its own duration when the variable is unset. The integration suite itself runs on local folders only. Each run works under a random prefix in the bucket and removes it at the end. Use a dedicated, empty bucket, and set up credentials as described in vignette("locations"):

withr::with_envvar(
  c(RCS_TEST_LEVEL = "full", RCS_TEST_GCS = "gs://my-test-bucket"),
  devtools::test()
)

Without RCS_TEST_GCS, and on CRAN, these tests are skipped.

Coverage 

covr::package_coverage()

The aim is at least 90% of lines overall and 80% in every file.
